Scenario: Query contains no recognized product category noun (e.g., 'black slim fit cotton')
Detection: Category token detector returns null or 0 matches against category taxonomy.
Expected_Behavior: Do not drop any token arbitrarily. Fall back to multi-field fuzzy text search with BM25 coordinate matching. If still < 3, show category recommendation fallback.

Scenario: All tokens appear equally selective / identical document frequency
Detection: Token frequency variance < 0.05 across all constituent query tokens.
Expected_Behavior: Drop the rightmost adjective/attribute token by positional convention, preserving token 1 (often gender/target) and final token if noun.

Scenario: Relaxing one token still produces zero results (N-1 tokens = 0 hits)
Expected_Behavior: Attempt single secondary relaxation to N-2 tokens only if query >= 5 tokens; otherwise stop and render graceful empty state with trending items.

Scenario: Brand + Category specific query with 0 results (e.g., 'Nike cashmere formal blazer')
Detection: NER identifies explicit Brand entity alongside incompatible Category entity.
Expected_Behavior: Brand entity is locked (never dropped). Relaxation removes fabric/style modifier ('cashmere' or 'formal'), searching for Nike blazers.

Scenario: Size / Color combination over-constrains stock (e.g., 'XXL neon yellow silk top')
Detection: Size and color tokens identified, but inventory matrix has 0 available SKUs.
Expected_Behavior: Preserve category and color; drop size token with explicit banner: 'Showing neon yellow silk tops in all available sizes'.

Scenario: Query contains obvious typo (e.g., 'men blck cotton shrt')
Detection: Token spellchecker flags edit distance 1 from known catalog words.
Expected_Behavior: Apply typo correction before relaxation logic. If corrected query yields >= 3 hits, return corrected results without dropping attributes.

Scenario: Query contains duplicate or redundant tokens (e.g., 'men shirt cotton casual shirt')
Detection: Set length of normalized tokens < total token count.
Expected_Behavior: Deduplicate tokens during query normalization step prior to strict search execution.

Scenario: Extremely long query (>= 8 tokens, e.g. conversational cut-and-paste text)
Expected_Behavior: Extract top 4 most salient entities (Gender, Category, Color, Brand) using entity extractor; execute search on core 4 tokens.

Scenario: Catalog database temporarily degraded / slow response
Detection: Primary search execution latency exceeds 120 ms circuit breaker threshold.
Expected_Behavior: Bypass query relaxation fallback immediately; return available strict matches or fast cached empty state to protect p95 latency.

Scenario: Fallback retrieval service times out or throws unhandled exception
Detection: Relaxation API returns HTTP 500 or timeout > 50 ms.
Expected_Behavior: Catch exception gracefully in gateway; log error; return original strict results to client without breaking UI.

Scenario: Shopper rapidly reformulates before relaxed results render
Detection: Subsequent query issued within < 1.5 seconds of previous search ID.
Expected_Behavior: Cancel in-flight relaxation request for previous search ID via client abort signal; process latest query immediately.

Scenario: Shopper clicks 'Search anyway for exact [Original Query]'
Expected_Behavior: Bypass relaxation logic completely; execute pure strict search and render exact result count (even if 0) without fallback.

Scenario: Adult, offensive, or prohibited search terms
Detection: Token matches automated content moderation blocklist.
Expected_Behavior: Bypass relaxation entirely; return zero results with standard neutral messaging; log moderation flag.

Scenario: Query contains stop words only or low-signal terms (e.g. 'the best of in')
Detection: All tokens flagged as stop words in English language dictionary.
Expected_Behavior: Do not attempt attribute relaxation; return standard curated popular landing page.

Scenario: User repeatedly bounces from relaxed results (quick-back clicks)
Detection: Session logs >= 2 consecutive PDP views with duration < 5s on relaxed results.
Expected_Behavior: Demote relaxed candidate rankings for remainder of session; prioritize user refinement chips.

Scenario: Strict search yields exactly 1 or 2 results (Subgroup B: 43 queries)
Expected_Behavior: Display the 1-2 exact matches at top of grid labeled 'Exact Matches', followed by section header 'You may also like these close matches' with relaxed items.
